circumstances: The researcher executes the bounded replication defined on Day 18. The corrected preprocessing passes checks and the full run completes, but the reproduced result is weaker than reported in the reference paper. Before interpreting this as a failure to reproduce, the researcher checks the reference implementation and discovers that the paper's reported comparison appears to use a slightly different evaluation subset than the main-text description implies. The researcher does not immediately alter the replication. Instead, they document the discrepancy, compare the available metadata, and conclude that one controlled follow-up is justified before deciding whether the replication should be abandoned. The day is experiment-heavy with a long monitoring period, a short break, and limited unrelated browsing.

activities.title: Run and inspect the bounded replication
activities.summary: The researcher verified the corrected preprocessing, launched the bounded replication with the predefined seed, waited for completion, and analyzed headline metrics, confidence intervals, and subgroup outputs. The reproduced result was weaker than the reference result.

activities.title: Investigate why the replication differs from the reference
activities.summary: The researcher revisited the paper and supplementary material and found evidence that the evaluation subset reconstructed locally may not match the subset underlying the reported result. The discrepancy was documented rather than silently changing the replication setup.

label_notes.context: Unexpected replication result required interpretation before any further run.

activities.title: Quantify the evaluation-subset discrepancy
activities.summary: The researcher revised the replication decision criteria, compared reconstructed subset counts, searched later studies for discussion of evaluation choices, and recorded unresolved assumptions. No full rerun was launched.

label_notes.context: Follow-up analysis of the reference implementation ambiguity.

activities.title: Define a controlled replication follow-up
activities.summary: After a brief personal search, the researcher defined one controlled evaluation-subset comparison and an explicit stopping rule, then prepared analysis cells without running the follow-up yet.

key_observations: The bounded replication completed successfully from a software and preprocessing perspective, but its headline result was weaker than the reference paper's reported result.
The difference cannot yet be interpreted as a straightforward replication failure because the reference paper's evaluation-subset description appears underspecified.
The researcher avoided silently changing the replication to obtain a closer result and instead documented the reconstruction discrepancy.
A controlled evaluation-subset comparison is now justified, but it is explicitly bounded by a stopping rule.
The replication has become a methodological investigation rather than a simple reproduction task.
priority_alignment: The day's main priority was the bounded replication and interpretation of its result.
Literature searching was used to investigate a concrete evaluation ambiguity rather than to broaden the research question.
No new benchmark or unrelated experiment program was started.
important_uncertainty: It is unclear whether matching the reference evaluation subset will materially change the replication result.
The supplementary material does not completely eliminate ambiguity about how the reported subset was constructed.
Even if the result changes, the scientific value of continuing the replication remains uncertain.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Run the single controlled evaluation-subset comparison, compare it directly with the original replication, and stop if the discrepancy cannot be explained without introducing additional undocumented assumptions.

things_not_to_do: Do not alter multiple preprocessing or evaluation choices simultaneously.
Do not treat the weaker result as proof that the reference paper is incorrect.
Do not keep adding reconstruction variants after the predefined subset comparison if the discrepancy remains unexplained.
Do not restart the main submitted manuscript project solely because the replication result differs.
